Answer: B
Reason: The lateral chest X-ray (Figure 1) shows a large, homogeneous, well-circumscribed opacity that forms an obtuse angle with the chest wall, which is a classic radiographic sign of an extrapulmonary (pleural or chest wall) mass rather than an intrapulmonary lesion. This finding is confirmed by the CT scans (Figures 2 and 3), which demonstrate a large, well-defined pleural-based mass.
